steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Mr. Ji.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Ah... you must be young Lord Zuo.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Alas, where are my manners? I didn't even prepare a gift for our first meeting.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You know me?

steps.name: Strange Fabric
steps.text: (Eerie wail)
Zuo Le reflexively reaches for his sword, but finds only a Tianshi apparatus for controlling agricultural instruments on his belt.
His movement did not escape the man's attention. The corners of the man's mouth rise up slightly.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: No need to be nervous, Lord Zuo. These are but harmless toys.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: 'Weave cause to effect, cut unreal into real'... are these your creations?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Just doing my part.

steps.name: Strange Fabric
steps.text: (Eerie cry)
The man waves his hand, and the strange creature turns to tiny threads before vanishing.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The ways of the Feranmut proxies are mystifying.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Petty parlor tricks. Not much use to them.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Pestilence and blight tend to follow a flood. Dealing with disaster you can't see or touch is hard; weave it into an object, and it becomes easier to deal with.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: My elder sister would chastise me for violating the laws of nature, if she saw me do this.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You shouldn't be here.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: This is my childhood home, after all. I got a little homesick.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I didn't know your kind had childhoods.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: We were all ignorant once, no matter how long our lifespans. New things left a deeper impression on us.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: And we think more about those who around us, at the time.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Any meeting of you and your siblings is an important matter that should have been reported to the Sui Regulator in advance.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: The imperial court's convoy was delayed by Catastrophe. I got word from the old Tianshi and immediately sent relief supplies out of my own pocket.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: I only saw my older sister briefly and haven't even caught a glimpse of the younger ones. Isn't the Sui Regulator being a little, you know, inbhumane?

spans.text: I only saw my older sister briefly and haven't even caught a glimpse of the younger ones. Isn't the Sui Regulator being a little, you know,

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The Sui Regulator has instructions to keep a close eye on you.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Even though I've never broken a single rule in all these years?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: It is not up to you.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: And yet, you're not wearing the garb of a Candleholder.
The man smiles. His demeanor is gentle, polite, relaxed.
But Zuo Le cannot help but feel a chill up his spine.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: I have heard much about you, Lord Zuo. That we should meet here is certainly the will of Heaven, and I would very much like to make your acquaintance.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: There's no need to flatter me.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: I've seen many a scion of blue-blood families in Baizao, plenty of them intelligent and learned.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: But it would be a challenge to find more than a handful who could get down to business and do honest work like you.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: In the eleventh month of last year, you entered the den of the Langyi Shanhaizhong by yourself and rescued dozens of innocent prisoners.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: In the second month of this year, you braved numerous dangers in pursuit of that special goblet.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: The uninformed believed you to have risen to your position at such a young age because of your father. What do they know of the dangers of a Candleholder's duty?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Why should one mistake wipe out all the hard work you've done in the past?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You're not supposed to know of these things.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Ah, a businessman hears many things. After all, the things one hears can be a commodity, too, if another is willing to pay a price for them.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: And it's my business to know what kind of customer would pay what kind of price for information.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: For example, I know what's on the other side of the river to the north of Dahuang. I know what Nian is building here.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: I know you suspect that ulterior motives were involved in the Catastrophe that struck Yumen, but all your leads came up empty. Am I right?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Your meticulousness is impressive.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: But I would not underestimate the Sui Regulator, if I were you. We will get to the bottom of any suspicions we have.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I would caution you to toe the line.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Is this a word of advice from a friend?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: A word of warning from a Candleholder of the Sui Regulator.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: I'm sure you worry too much. The best Tianshis in all of Yan are all gathered in the Chamber of Heaven's Designs north of Dahuang. What can one little man do?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Should you not be more concerned about the... things across the river?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Do you know how many Tianshis the Chamber of Heaven's Designs has lost in the past three months?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Don't you dare spread lies and rumors...

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Trust is a merchant's greatest asset. I never lie, Lord Zuo. You can look into it yourself, if you don't believe it.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Then, think about what you want to do, and whether it might involve a deal with me.
Everything is just as usual.
The wind is silent.
Stockbeasts bury their heads in the grass.
The girl looks around.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Stupid Mianmian. How many times have I told him not to run away?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Stupid Xiaohe. He doesn't even remember my song! I'm not playing with him anymore!
Layer after layer of leaves block out the sky. The wind brings with it the pleasant scent of rice.
The earth is damp, and she leaves footprints in it as she steps upon it, walking forward while brushing aside the leaves that hide the skies.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Mianmian! It's time to go home!

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Mianmian! Why did you run away? Get back to your pen, or I'm gonna get scolded along with you.
A gentle breeze brushes by. The large, dark eyes of the stockbeast reflect the skies, the clouds, and the fields.
Grain Buds sees her own reflection in those eyes.

steps.name: Stockbeast's Voice
steps.text: I'm going away.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Stockbeast's Voice
steps.text: I don't want to eat grass anymore.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Has Xiaohe been putting weird stuff in your fodder again?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: I'll talk to him, and make sure you guys are eating properly!

steps.name: Stockbeast's Voice
steps.text: It's scary here.

steps.name: Stockbeast's Voice
steps.text: Death is coming.

steps.name: Stockbeast's Voice
steps.text: Will you come with us?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: You mean the flood a few days ago?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: No need to be scared. The flood is gone. I'll build tougher houses for you, so you won't have to be afraid when Catastrophe comes! I'll protect you!

steps.name: Stockbeast's Voice
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Stockbeast's Voice
steps.text: It comes from across the river.

steps.name: Stockbeast's Voice
steps.text: Look beneath your feet.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Beneath... what...?
Grain Buds sees her own reflection in those eyes.
A gentle breeze brushes by. The large, dark eyes of the stockbeast reflect the skies, the clouds, and the fields.
The girl looks around.
Stockbeasts bury their heads in the grass.
The wind is silent.
Everything is just as usual.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Uncle Wang? What are you doing?

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: Moving trees.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: The peace tree? It was in perfectly good shape. Why are you moving it? What about those Tumu Tianshis?

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: Give me a hand and move that dirt over there... they've gone back to the factories. They'll be transporting materials through here in a bit.

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: Everyone knows that there's no saving this land.

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: Xiaohe, you're a student at the Tianshi Bureau, but you're also from around here. Tell us, what's happened to the land?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I... I don't know...

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: ...Hmph.

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: Yeah, I know, every inch of land is business to the mandarins. How much money it takes to turn them into moving plates, and how much money they stand to make.

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: But this is our home! My family has lived here for generations!

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: How could they tell us to abandon our home just like that!

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: This is my home too.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I promise I'll get to the bottom of what's happening here. I'll find a way to save the land...

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: What use are your promises? They promised to take these fields along when they started building the nomadic city.

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: Fine, I'll pretend I lost the land to a Catastrophe, but I'm taking this tree with me.

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: My grandpa's grandma planted it. The people in the cities think home is something you can take with you. Well, this tree is my home, and I'm taking it with me.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: ...I'll help.
The old farmer lifts the peace tree onto his shoulder. Carrying his home, he leaves deep footprints in the mud.
He Sheng looks back at the core city as he carries the heavy tree.
The lumberjack looks down, a blank expression on his face.
After a period of silence, he opens his mouth.

steps.name: Silent Lumberjack
steps.text: Are you looking for something?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: You can talk?

steps.name: Silent Lumberjack
steps.text: What are you doing here?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: My stockbeast ran away. I came to bring him back.

steps.name: Silent Lumberjack
steps.text: What stockbeast?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Right here—
She points to her side.
The water underneath her feet reflects her figure, the clouds, the sky.
There is straw all around, but no sign of any animal.
She blinks.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: ...I could have sworn he was here.

steps.name: Silent Lumberjack
steps.text: Follow me.

steps.name: Silent Lumberjack
steps.text: I'll help you find your stockbeast.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Have a seat, Lord Zuo.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: ...Assistant Minister Ning.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: What a coincidence.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: From Shangshu to Yumen, and now to Dahuang. You must be an outstanding Candleholder to be handed such responsibility.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What are your instructions?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Please, no need for such formality.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I would not be meeting you here, if this was official business. There is a matter that requires your assistance in a... less than official manner.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: About the Sui proxies?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: The Twelve Pagodas and Five Cities project is of crucial importance to Great Yan. Having four proxies here in the same place, at a time like this, is a headache to say the least.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: There may be devastating consequences if someone with ulterior motives decides to cause trouble.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Do you mean to say that you already know someone intends to cause trouble?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Are you aware that the development of Dahuang has resumed?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The trader's supplies... he should not interfere with such matters.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: All I know is that he had a meeting with Assistant Minister Wan from the Ministry of Works. Do you know him?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I'm familiar with him... he has been working on Dahuang's mobile plate development in recent years, but he also participated in Yumen's repairs a few months ago.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What is Ji planning?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Ji was known to be close to Shu, and the two of them used to farm Dahuang a thousand years ago. Ji later left Dahuang to start a business.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: He returns to Dahuang once every few decades. The last visit was sixty years ago.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You recall these details well...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Do you suspect that he intends to sabotage Dahuang?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Right now, we need to figure out why he came back to Dahuang. This is what I would like you to uncover.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The Ministry of Rites and the Sui Regulator have long been at odds over the Sui issue. Yet now you're asking me to do this.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Where do you stand yourself?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: As a Candleholder, my duty is to my orders, of course...

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: You want to be a good sword.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: That way, it's not the sword's fault, even if it kills the wrong person.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I'm not trying to shirk responsibility—

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Have you ever thought about why the Sui Regulator wants to eliminate the Sui by force?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: If there comes a day when Yumen goes to the capital, ending the existence of both cities and the Feranmut to the sound of cannonfire...

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Do we really say 'We had no choice' about all the people who lose their homes and the soldiers who lose their lives?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Was there really no other way?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What prompts you to ask me to do this?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: The welfare of the people. Not the cloaks and daggers of the court.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Honesty and integrity. I'm sure the answer is right there in your heart.
The man points at the calm surface of the river, smooth like a mirror, almost like it has frozen in place.
The water reflects the clouds in the sky, and the girl's face.

steps.name: Silent Lumberjack
steps.text: The stockbeast is inside.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: In the river?

steps.name: Silent Lumberjack
steps.text: You want to find him, go down.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: I'll find him down there and bring him back to his pen.
The river channel booms with the sound of crashing water and roiling air.
The girl steps forward.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Come back! You'll die!
The old lumberjack suddenly raises his axe high, before putting it back down meekly.

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: Let me go, Zushi! I'll bring her back!

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: I know how to handle it. She's not that far gone. Let me go, and I can bring her back!

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: Zushi, no! She can still be saved!

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: Zushiiiiiiii—!

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: There is only death there. She's beyond all help. You can't save her.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Go back. Put up a grave monument.

steps.name: Annoyed Girl
steps.text: Where do you think you're going, you idiot?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: The stockbeast is down there. The old lumberjack told me so. I'm bringing him back.

steps.name: Annoyed Girl
steps.text: You're the stockbeast, you dumb rice-brain!

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Are you talking about me?!

steps.name: Annoyed Girl
steps.text: Of course I'm talking about you! You think there's a stockbeast down there? Are you blind or stupid?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Oh, shut up—
Splat!
A piece of river mud hits Grain Buds in the face.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Whoa!

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Pfft, bleh, argh!
Her sight remains surprisingly clear. She still sees everything before her.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: What's going on?
Grain Buds tries to wipe the mud away, but there is something hard in the mud that sticks to her face.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Why are there two pieces of...?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Rice?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Uncle?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Where's the mute uncle?

steps.name: Annoyed Girl
steps.text: What uncle? All I see is you trying to jump into the water, you crazy idiot!

steps.name: Annoyed Girl
steps.text: Now throw that away!
Grain Buds washes away the mud by the river.
The angry girl turns around. There is nobody in the forest beyond the levee, but she stares long and hard into the woods and nods.
The footsteps grow distant, disappearing amongst the trees.

a.text: '...has violated the statutes by entering Dahuang and meeting proxies without permission. The penalties hereof are temporary deferred in consideration of his assistance to the disaster relief efforts.
'It is hereby ordered that... depart Dahuang within three days under the supervision of the Sui Regulator... any delays will be subject to strict penalties.'

steps.text: The red-stamped letter sits prominently at the center of the table. It seems that whoever placed it here knew when the master of the room would return, and how she would react.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: You wouldn't tell it to my face?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: You say you trust me, but will we ever have a chance to sit down and talk to each other again?
